extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent applicants / patent attorneys practising under the Korean Patent Act
extracted.subtask_description: Examination guidance on determining identicalness/enlarged novelty, first-to-file disputes, reference dates, and handling conflicting (prior-filed/later-filed) applications under the Korean Patent Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of Determination of Identicalness
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining of applying Article 29 paragraph (3) and (4) refers to whether an invention described in the claimed invention is identical to the invention or utility innovation specified in the description or drawings in another application at its filing (hereinafter referred to as 'prior art reference').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (1) Determine a claimed invention of the present application (same as novelty determination in Chapter 2). (2) Determine the disclosure of the prior art reference from the specification description (including inherent disclosure obvious in light of common general knowledge). (3) Find identicalness and difference by comparing the claimed invention with the prior art reference (do not compare claimed invention with an invention formed by combining more than two prior art references). (4) If no difference between subject matters defining the claimed invention and prior art reference, they are identical; identicalness includes substantial identicalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial Method of Determination of Identicalness
rubrics_metrics.description: Identicalness of invention is related with determining novelty as well as inventive step (Article 29(2)), disclosure exception (Article 30), enlarged concept of novelty (Article 29(3),(4)), protection of lawful holder of a right, first-to-file, succession to rights, divisional/converted applications and priority claims; the criteria of identicalness shall apply in those cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply identicalness criteria consistently across related Articles; determining identicalness relies on comparing subject matter-defining elements of claimed invention and prior art reference. If there is any difference in subject matter, the inventions are not identical. Complete or substantial identity results in being identical to a prior art reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where inventions are substantially identical
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions are substantially identical where only non-substantial matters (secondary matters), not the technical ideas, are different — e.g., simple differences in expression, recognition of effects, purposes or use, simple change in configuration, or simple differences in usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination under Article 29(3) considers identicalness of technical configuration and effects. Even if technical configurations differ, if differences are only detailed means (mere addition/deletion/change of prior arts) that do not create new effects, the inventions are deemed substantially identical. Example: case law (2006 Hu 1452) supports this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference in Expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in expression refer to expressions used in patent claims being different but contents substantially the same; such category differences treated as differences in expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The method of desalination of sea water' vs 'the method of concentration of sea water' by separating water through insertion of a refrigerant undissolved in sea water — considered difference in expression when substantive content is same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference in Recognition of Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in recognition of effects occur when recognition of effects of the inventions is different even though the effects are identical because configurations are identical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: prior-filed application discloses greater electric insulation; later-filed discloses better high frequency properties — same configuration but different stated recognition of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference in Purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in purposes refer to subjective purposes of the inventions being different even though configurations are the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only the stated purpose differs but the technical configuration is the same, treat as non-substantial difference for identicalness analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in Configurations — general
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes in configurations refer to cases where configuration of the invention is changed and becomes another invention; where such changes constitute mere substitution, addition or deletion of technical means that could be easily made by a person skilled in the art and do not lead to significant changes in purposes/effects, they are treated as non-substantial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of such changes include 'mere change of means', 'mere addition or deletion of means', 'mere change of material or substitution of equivalents', 'mere change of equal means', 'mere limitation or change of figures, numbers or sequence', and 'mere limitation or change of figures'. These are treated as non-substantial for identicalness if they don't change main purposes/effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere Change of Means
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere change of means refers to configuration change where the invention becomes another invention, but changes do not lead to significant differences in purposes/effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: clarifying fruit juice using bentonite then vacuum freeze drying vs using diatomite then vacuum freeze drying — considered mere change of means if purposes/effects unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere Addition or Deletion of Means
rubrics_metrics.description: Mere addition or deletion of means refers to configuration changes (addition/deletion) that do not lead to significant differences in purposes/effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided (chemical manufacturing processes) to show addition/deletion that is considered mere change; judge whether change materially alters technical solution or effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere Change of Material or Mere Substitution of Equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to changes constituting substitution of materials or articles having comparability or same function that do not lead to significant differences in purposes/effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a foundation pile with blades attached on the concrete shack vs blades on the shack pile — treated as mere substitution if functionally equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere Change of Equal Means
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to changes of means having comparability or the same function that do not lead to significant differences in purposes/effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether substituted means are functionally equivalent to determine non-substantiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere Limitation or Change of Figures, Numbers or Sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to changes that are mere limitation or change of figures, numbers or sequences a person skilled in the art would commonly apply, not leading to significant differences in purposes/effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes mere limitation or change of figures; treat as non-substantial where they are routine adjustments by skilled person based on purpose and other configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differences in Mere Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences in mere uses refer to cases where two inventions have different uses but these differences derive from differences in other configurations and are not substantive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A plasticizer of PVC comprising compound B' vs 'A ultraviolet light absorber of PVC comprising compound B' — difference in use but same substantive configuration; similarly, spraying chemical A to repel hares vs deer — mere use difference if configuration same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of Use Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Existence of mere limitation of uses refers to differences being marked as whether uses are limited or not, where such use limitations are clearly derived from other configurations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'A net comprising threads with flat cross sections' vs 'A fish net comprising threads with flat cross sections' — the 'fish' limitation may be a mere use limitation if derived from other configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-File Rule (Article 36) — entitlement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where at least two patent applications for an identical invention are filed on different dates, only the applicant of the application having the earlier filing date is entitled to a patent on the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 36 establishes the first-to-file system; it applies mutatis mutandis between patent applications and utility model applications when inventions are identical. The rule aims to prevent double patenting and multiple exclusivities for the same technical idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-File Rule — same filing date (agreement requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where at least two patent applications for an identical invention are filed on the same date, only the person agreed upon by all patent applicants may obtain a patent; if applicants fail or are unable to reach agreement, none obtains a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner may order applicants to report results of agreement within a specified period; failure to report is deemed failure to reach agreement. Procedures exist for reporting change of right relation (Annexed Form No.20) and conducting consequent proceedings such as withdrawal of conflicting applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications deemed never filed under Article 36(4) and (5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be deemed never filed for purposes of Article 36(1)-(3) if (1) the application is abandoned, invalidated, or withdrawn, or (2) a decision/trial decision to reject becomes final and conclusive. Also, an application filed by a person who is neither inventor nor lawful successor shall be deemed never filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if a decision/trial decision to reject becomes final but paragraph (2) proviso applies, the application may still hold status as prior-filed (applies to applications filed after March 3, 2006). This prevents applicants from refiling after adverse final decisions to circumvent first-to-file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Requirement — Identical Invention determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The identicalness of the invention shall be determined based on whether the claimed inventions in the applications have the same technical ideas (including invention vs utility innovation). Where more than two claims exist, identicalness is determined per claim. Article 36 applies regardless of identicalness of inventors or applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination process: (i) specify inventions disclosed in claims (same as Chapter 2 novelty process); (ii) identify identicalness and differences by comparison; (iii) if no difference in configurations, deemed identical; if differences exist but fall under enlarged concept of novelty (Chapter 4 para 6), deemed the same (including substantial identicalness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications lacking status as prior-filed application
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application or utility model registration application that is invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, or where a final rejection exists does not hold status as a prior-filed application. Also, an application filed by a person who is neither an inventor/utility innovator nor a successor in title shall not hold prior-filed status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: exception where final decision to reject falls under the latter sentence of Article 36(2) — such applications may still hold prior-filed status (applies to filings after March 3, 2006). Examine whether grounds for decision violate first-to-file to prevent refiling abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of Reference Date — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date used to determine earliest filing or same-date status is recognized as follows depending on priority and filing circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See subrules for specific categories (no priority, treaty priority, domestic priority, divisional/converted, lawful holder/misappropriated, international applications pre-/post-2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date — application without priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date of an application without priority shall be the actual filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple rule: actual filing date is used when no priority claim exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date — application with treaty priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date of an application with priority claim under a treaty on an invention disclosed in the specification or drawings of the application serving as the basis of the priority claim shall be the filing date of the application which is the basis of the priority claim. For multiple priority claims, reference date is the earliest filing date among the filing dates of each invention. Markush-type claims may have different reference dates even within the same claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply per-invention earliest priority date. Note Markush group considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date — domestic priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date of an application with domestic priority on an invention disclosed in the specification or drawings of the application serving as the basis of the prior-filed application shall be the filing date of that prior application. For multiple domestic priority claims, the earliest filing date among each invention applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same per-invention earliest-date rule as treaty priority; note Markush-type implications as above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date — divisional and converted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date of a divisional application and converted application shall be the filing date of the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional/converted inherit the original application's filing date for first-to-file and priority determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date — application filed by lawful holder of a right (misappropriation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reference date of an application filed by a lawful holder of a right shall be the filing date of a misappropriated application; the misappropriated application shall be deemed to have never been filed and its reference date shall not be acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lawful holder's filing references the misappropriated application's filing date; misappropriated application itself treated as never filed for reference-date acknowledgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date — international applications filed on/before Dec 31, 2014
rubrics_metrics.description: For international patent applications (Republic of Korea designated state) filed on/before Dec 31, 2014, the reference date shall be the filing date of the international patent application on an invention disclosed in the translation of the specification, claims or drawings of the international patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications considered to be a patent application by decision (Article 214(4)), reference date is filing date of invention disclosed in the translation under Article 214(4) or Utility Model Act Article 40(4). Translation requirement applicable pre-2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference date — international applications filed on/after Jan 1, 2015
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications (ROK designated state) filed on/after Jan 1, 2015, 'laid open to public inspection' refers to PCT Article 21 international publication; reference date shall be the date of filing the international application on an invention disclosed in the specification or drawings of the international application (no Korean-translation prerequisite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying Article 29(3) and (4) to international applications claiming domestic priority, inventions disclosed in the specification or drawings submitted at the international filing date are used as the reference for enlarged novelty and identicalness analyses. International applications deemed withdrawn for failure to submit Korean translation under Article 214(4) cannot be relied upon as another application under Article 29(3) and (4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination where more than two applications filed on different dates — examiner handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple applications for the same invention are filed on different dates, only the earliest filing may obtain a patent. Examiners must handle later-filed applications according to applicant identity and publication status of prior-filed applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant and inventor differ and prior-filed application is laid open or registered, Article 29(3) and (4) apply to later-filed application; proviso on enlarged novelty can be flexibly applied even if claims not confirmed. If prior-filed not laid open, postpone examination until it is laid open/registered. If applicants/inventors are same, apply Article 36 proviso and make decision after scope of claims in prior-filed application is confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination where more than two applications filed on same date — procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple applications for same invention are filed on the same date, only the person agreed upon by all applicants may obtain a patent; if no agreement, none obtains a patent. Consultation/reporting and subsequent proceedings are required when agreement reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report on change of right relation (Annexed Form No.20) must be submitted when agreement reached; withdrawal or other proceedings should follow. Applicants may avoid rejection by amending/deleting conflicting invention via amendment without consultation. Treatment of patent vs utility model registrations on same date follows same rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation on Conflicting Applications — initial checks
rubrics_metrics.description: When conflicting applications are found, examiners should check whether the patent applicant is identical and whether conflicting application is invalidated, withdrawn, abandoned, finally rejected, or filed by an unentitled person; such conflicting applications cannot hold prior-filed status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conflicting application lacks prior-filed status, examiner treats it as never filed. Note: conflicting applications with different applicants/inventors are rare; often result from incorrect claim amendments when filing divisionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when applicant is different (consultation and notification procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: If conflicting application applicant is different and a conflicting application is granted or laid open, examiner should notify the present applicant of the conflicting relation and either request consultation (if conflicting application requested examination) or postpone examination until conflicting application is requested for examination or withdrawn/abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a request for consultation is made, examiner notifies grounds for rejection under Article 36(2)/(3), and after applicant reports result of consultation and remedies within designated period, examiner shall grant patent; otherwise, issue decision to reject. If conflicting app is not yet laid open/requested, notify intention to postpone examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling when applicant is identical (examiner actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicants are identical and a conflicting application is granted a patent or finally rejected, the examiner shall issue a notice of rejection under Article 36(2) or (3). If conflicting application is not yet granted, notify other grounds for rejection to the applicant without reviewing Article 36(2)/(3); if those other grounds remain unremedied after amendment, reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notified grounds are remedied but the conflicting application's consequence (grant/rejection) is undecided at reexamination, a patent may be granted to the present application unless the conflicting application is later granted; examiners must coordinate outcomes between conflicting applications.
